pages.title: Glossary · Tomas Korcak
pages.description: The 48 terms this site explains itself with: languages, technologies and concepts, each defined, sourced and linked to every page that uses it.

pages.title: AI agent (concept)
pages.description: A program that uses a language model to plan and act (edit code, run commands) toward a goal; Majordomus makes such agents prove their work.

pages.title: Alpine.js (technology)
pages.description: A small JavaScript framework that adds behaviour to HTML in its own attributes; here the filters, drawers and palette.

pages.title: Apache ECharts (technology)
pages.description: An Apache project for interactive charts: calendars, sunbursts, maps and large data sets.

pages.title: C (programming language)
pages.description: The small, fast systems language beneath operating systems and most other languages.

pages.title: Chart.js (technology)
pages.description: A light library for common charts (bars, lines, doughnuts) on an HTML canvas.

pages.title: Commit (concept)
pages.description: One recorded change in a repository, with its author and time; the last commit dates a project's activity here.

pages.title: C++ (programming language)
pages.description: C with classes, templates and abstractions that cost nothing at run time; used where speed matters.

pages.title: C# (programming language)
pages.description: Microsoft's object-oriented language for .NET. A term of the glossary.

pages.title: CSS (programming language)
pages.description: The style language of the web: layout, colour and typography of HTML.

pages.title: Cytoscape.js (technology)
pages.description: A library for drawing and analysing graphs (networks of nodes and edges) in the browser.

pages.title: D3.js (technology)
pages.description: Data-Driven Documents: a toolkit that binds data to SVG and HTML, the basis of the art visuals here (spiral, bubbles, streams).

pages.title: Data visualisation (concept)
pages.description: Turning numbers into pictures people can read at a glance: here spirals, bubbles, streams and graphs, each drawn from measured data.

pages.title: Dockerfile (programming language)
pages.description: The recipe that builds a container image: a base system, files and commands, reproducible anywhere.

pages.title: Elixir (programming language)
pages.description: A functional language on the Erlang virtual machine, built for concurrent, fault-tolerant systems.

pages.title: Erlang (programming language)
pages.description: A language and runtime from telecoms, designed for systems that must keep running while parts of them fail.

pages.title: Flowbite Pro (technology)
pages.description: A licensed library of interface blocks and an application shell on Tailwind CSS; every page of this site is built from it.

pages.title: Fork (concept)
pages.description: A copy of someone else's repository under your account; forks are counted on this site but never shown as the owner's work.

pages.title: Front matter (concept)
pages.description: Structured data at the top of a content file (here TOML) that describes the page to the generator and to machines.

pages.title: GIS (concept)
pages.description: Geographic information systems: data tied to places, stored, analysed and drawn as maps.

pages.title: GitHub Pages (technology)
pages.description: GitHub's hosting for static websites, deployed from a repository; this site and most project sites live there.

pages.title: Haskell (programming language)
pages.description: A purely functional language with lazy evaluation and a strong type system; a place to learn to think in types.

pages.title: HTML (programming language)
pages.description: The markup language of web pages: the structure that styles and scripts work on.

pages.title: Internationalisation (concept)
pages.description: Designing software so every text can be translated; this site exists in English and Czech, and a gate fails on any untranslated text.

pages.title: Java (programming language)
pages.description: An object-oriented language on the Java Virtual Machine, long the default of enterprise software.

pages.title: JavaScript (programming language)
pages.description: The programming language of the web browser, also run on servers through Node.js. Every interactive part of this site is JavaScript.

pages.title: MCP (technology)

pages.title: Mirror (concept)

pages.title: PostgreSQL (technology)
pages.description: An open-source relational database known for correctness and extensions.

pages.title: Python (programming language)
pages.description: A general-purpose language valued for readability, common in data work and scripting.

pages.title: Repository (concept)
pages.description: A project's folder under version control: its files and their whole history of commits.

pages.title: Ruby (programming language)
pages.description: A dynamic, expressive language designed for programmer happiness; many of the older tools here are Ruby.

pages.title: Rust (programming language)
pages.description: A systems language that guarantees memory safety without a garbage collector; Majordomus is written in it.

pages.title: Shell (programming language)
pages.description: Scripts for the Unix command line (bash, zsh), the glue that installs, builds and deploys.

pages.title: Static site generator (concept)
pages.description: A program that turns content and templates into plain files before anyone visits, so the site needs no server code.

pages.title: Swift (programming language)
pages.description: Apple's language for iOS and macOS applications. A term of the glossary.

pages.title: Tailwind CSS (technology)
pages.description: A CSS framework of small utility classes composed in the markup, compiled to only what a page uses.

pages.title: TypeScript (programming language)
pages.description: JavaScript with static types, checked before the code runs and compiled to plain JavaScript.

pages.title: WCAG (concept)
pages.description: The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines; every page here is checked against WCAG 2.2 level AA before it ships.

pages.title: Web Audio (technology)
pages.description: The browser API for generating, processing and analysing sound in real time.

pages.title: Zola (technology)
